text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
***GENERAL***
ALL PAPERS
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn said on Sunday that wage and pension increases will at elast match inflation next year.
- Reconciliation within the opposition Christian Democrat party was unsuccessful so far.
- Canadian Jacques Villeneuve won the 12th Hungarian Formula One Grand Prix.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The State Audit Office has reassessed its judgement on the Budapest Bank privatisation taking into consideration the Finance Ministry's stance.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs said Hungary's foreign policy has been consistent since 1989.
- Romanian Defense Minister Victor Babiuc cancelled a visit to Hungary giving no public explanation for the move.
- Social insurance may be run be a trio of state-appointed officials if the unions cannot agree on delegating representatives.
***BUSINESS***
ALL PAPERS
- Hungary's current account deficit stood for the first six months stood at $800 million at the end of June.
- Construction industry output grew 2.8 percent in June year-on-year.
- Oil and gas company MOL Rt suspended petrol purchases from its Tiszai refinery following reports that a corrosive petrol component damaged AC pumps in various car models in north Hungary.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- National broadcaster Antenna Hungaria will not be sold this year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Light industry output grew 1.8 percent in June year-on-year.
- German supermarket chain Spar will open a new outlet in Bekescsaba tomorrow.
- Mobile phone company Pannon GSM had a partial breakdown over the weekend.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Privatisation agency APV Rt sold 85 companies in the first half of this year at an average price of 225 percent of the face value.
-- Budapest newsroom +36 1 327 4040
